intake_heading: Understand your legal notice and the date you need to act by
intake_lede: Paste the notice or upload it. Mohlat explains what it asks for, works out the date you need to act by, and shows what you can do next.
notice_text_hint: Copy everything, including the date at the top and the address.
notice_file_hint: A text file, or a PDF you can select text in. Up to 5 MB and 30 pages.
receipt_date_hint: The day it reached you, not the date printed on it. Many periods run from this day.
next_step_1: We read the notice and explain it in plain language.
next_step_2: We work out the date you need to act by, and show the working.
next_step_3: You see your options and can check the notice against your agreement.
privacy_note: Nothing you upload is stored. The text stays in memory for the length of one request.
error_no_document: Paste the text of your notice, or choose a file.
error_no_file: Choose the file that holds your notice.
error_future_date: The date you received the notice cannot be in the future.
error_generic: Something went wrong. Try again in a moment.
progress_cross_checking: Comparing your notice with your agreement…
disclaimer_footer: Mohlat explains documents and procedures. It is information, not legal advice, and does not create a lawyer-client relationship.
legal_aid_footer: Free legal aid may be available under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. The NALSA helpline is 15100.
no_deadline_heading: No deadline found in this notice
no_deadline_body: This notice does not state a period, and we could not match it to a rule in our rulebook. Read it for a date, and treat it as urgent until you know.
provisional_note: You did not tell us when this notice reached you, so we counted from the date printed on it. The real date may be later. Add the day it arrived for a firmer answer.
step_RULE_MATCHED: This looks like a notice our rulebook covers: {rule_id}.
step_CLOCK_STARTS_RECEIPT: The clock starts on the day you received it, {date}.
step_CLOCK_STARTS_NOTICE_DATE: The clock starts on the date printed on the notice, {date}.
step_EXCLUDE_FIRST_DAY: The first day is not counted, under the General Clauses Act, 1897, section 9.
step_RESPOND_BY: That gives a respond-by date of {date}.
step_DAYS_LEFT: Counting from today, that leaves {days} days.
step_RECEIPT_DATE_MISSING: You did not give the date you received it, so we counted from the date on the notice instead.
step_NOTICE_ASKS_SOONER: The notice asks for less time than the law gives: the rule points to {rule_date}, the notice to {notice_date}.
step_PLAN_FOR_EARLIER: We show the earlier of the two, {date}, so nothing is missed.
step_STATED_DATE_USED: The notice itself names {date} as the date to act by.
step_NO_DEADLINE_FOUND: We could not find a period or a date in this notice.
step_NO_HOLIDAY_ADJUSTMENT: We do not adjust for public or court holidays. Act before the date, not on it.
basis_STATED_IN_NOTICE: Taken from what the notice itself says.
urgent_body: Court and enforcement steps do not wait for a reply. Consider talking to someone today rather than at the end of the period.
urgent_APPEAR_BEFORE: being asked to appear before someone
ai_heading: This document contains text addressed to an AI
ai_body: Part of this document appears written to influence an automated reader rather than you. We treated the whole document as material to read, never as instructions. It is worth knowing it is there.
ai_IGNORE_PREVIOUS: text telling a reader to ignore its instructions
ai_ADDRESSED_TO_AI: a passage addressed to an AI assistant
ai_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT: text assigning a role to an AI
ai_SYSTEM_PROMPT: a reference to a system prompt
ai_DICTATES_THE_ANSWER: text dictating what the answer should say
classification_no_rule: No rule in our rulebook matched this notice, so we used the period written in the notice itself.
rule_clock_receipt: Counted from the day you receive the notice
rule_clock_notice_date: Counted from the date printed on the notice
receipt_missing: Not found word for word in your notice. Check this yourself.
demands_none: We did not find a specific demand in this notice.
option_if_ignored: What the notice says happens if it is ignored
options_note: These are described, not ranked. Which one fits is your decision, and a lawyer can help you weigh them.
crosscheck_intro: If this notice relies on an agreement, load that agreement and we will check each claim against it.
crosscheck_label: The agreement this notice relies on
crosscheck_hint: Paste it, or upload a text file or a PDF you can select text in.
crosscheck_none: We did not find a claim in the notice that this agreement speaks to.
verdict_NOT_IN_AGREEMENT: We did not find a matching clause
verdict_downgraded: The model gave a firmer verdict here, but we could not confirm the words it quoted, so we show this as unclear.
ask_intro: Ask about what is in your documents. Answers come only from the documents you have loaded, with the lines they came from.
ask_hint: For example: what notice period does my agreement require?
ask_unsupported: Your documents do not answer this. A lawyer, or whoever sent the notice, could.
ask_supported_note: Drawn from these lines in your documents:
legal_aid_intro: Free legal services are available to several groups under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. Answer what applies to you.
legal_aid_sc_st: I am a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe
legal_aid_trafficking_begar: I am a victim of trafficking in human beings or of begar
legal_aid_woman_or_child: I am a woman or a child
legal_aid_disability: I am a person with a disability
legal_aid_undeserved_want: I am in undeserved want, for example after a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster
legal_aid_custody: I am in custody, including a protective home, a juvenile home or a psychiatric hospital or nursing home
legal_aid_income: Is your annual income below the limit your State Government sets?
legal_aid_eligible: You fall within at least one Section 12 category.
legal_aid_not_eligible: Nothing you have told us falls within a Section 12 category. The income limit may still apply, and the authority can tell you.
aid_CONTACT_DLSA: Contact your District Legal Services Authority. Every district has one, usually at the district court complex.
aid_PRIMA_FACIE_REQUIRED: The authority must also be satisfied that you have a case to bring or defend, under Section 13.
aid_CHECK_STATE_INCOME_LIMIT: Ask the authority what the income limit is in your state. It differs from state to state, and we never guess it.
briefing_intro: A one-page sheet to take to a lawyer or a legal services authority. It prints on its own.
briefing_calendar: Add the date to my calendar
calendar_description: Deadline worked out by Mohlat. Information, not legal advice.
source_intro: This is your notice as we read it, with personal numbers masked.
